shots.what: the fist sends the ball off, a burst behind (slow motion)
the ball hits the net, which bulges, swish lines
freeze on his face and the fist, which glows; a sly grin
a whip pan from the box to the stand, everything streaks
the packed stand, fans waving, the number standing gold on the pitch
match play, small players running on a sunny pitch
push in on the old clock board in the stand
low behind Maradona and two team-mates walking up the pitch
god's-eye over the pitch, both teams take their places
the two line-ups, the camera slides from blue to white
the ball drops toward him in the box
his left foot swings, the ball loops up and back over him
the camera flies beside the looping ball, a dotted trail behind it
Shilton on his line, ready
Shilton runs at the camera off his line, speed lines
both go up for the dropping ball, from a little wider
low behind him as he rises, slow motion
the top of the leap, both in the air, the ball on his fist
freeze, the fist meets the ball, a comic burst behind
the freeze, close on the fist and the glove a hand's width short; a ring draws on
from below, the ball drifts over the keeper's glove against the sky
Shilton looks up as the ball goes over him toward the goal
at grass level, the ball comes down toward the open goal
inside the post, the ball in the net, the net bulges
a whip to England's players, who turn with a start
they run at the camera, shouting
behind the referee, the England players point at their hands
calm, he points back to the centre circle
the replay on a 1980s TV in a living room, an orange arrow draws on
Maradona wheels away, arms wide, the crowd goes up
the press room, journalists' heads in front, flashes

the bunch of microphones, his grin above them
the leap again, as he remembers it (warm tint), the head near the ball
his head glows
pull back, the glow fades
the frozen contact once more, the camera turns around it
the fist glows gold
looking up past the raised fist into the sun, rays come down
the clock board turns from 51' to 55'
Maradona sets off with the ball, a puff of dust
god's-eye, an orange line draws his run toward the goal

crane up over the box, the gold words standing on the grass
